name: Gödel's Second Incompleteness Theorem

VINIT.justification: Pre-formal void before any statement or proof is named

TANCH.justification: Closes the system at the boundary where internal consistency becomes unprovable

AFWD.justification: Forward morphism from axioms to theorems via inference rules

AREV.justification: Reverse morphism tracing a theorem back to axioms to check for contradiction

CLINK.justification: Sequential composition of inference steps into a valid derivation sequence

IMSCRIB.justification: Self-reference mechanism mapping syntax to Gödel numbers, enabling the system to refer to itself

FSPLIT.justification: Branches the language into [Provable, Unprovable] paths based on derivability

FFUSE.justification: Reconstitutes the original formal language from both branches, satisfying FFUSE(FSPLIT(x))=x

EVALT.justification: Affirmative branch: assumes the Gödel sentence is derivable within the system

EVALF.justification: Negative branch: assumes the Gödel sentence is not derivable within the system

ENGAGR.justification: Paradice: simultaneously true in meta-theory and unprovable in object theory, held without resolution

IFIX.justification: Permanent record: the meta-fact that consistency cannot be proven internally

phase_3.false_description: Statement formally unprovable within the formal system
phase_3.both_description: Gödel sentence G: simultaneously true in meta-theory and unprovable in object theory

steps.domain_action: void formal system — initializes the empty axiomatic space before any statement is named
forward derivation — applies inference rules to generate theorems from axioms
chain inference — composes sequential proof steps into a valid derivation
diagonal self-reference — constructs the Gödel sentence G that asserts its own unprovability
provability bifurcation — branches the formal language into [Provable, Unprovable] paths
affirm provability — evaluates the T-arm assuming G is derivable
affirm unprovability — evaluates the F-arm assuming G is not derivable
reverse consistency trace — descends from assumed unprovability to axioms, revealing the consistency limit
paradice hold — simultaneously maintains truth of G in meta-theory and unprovability in object theory
meta-recovery — fuses branches to reconstitute the original formal system, exposing internal consistency limit
incompleteness record — permanently fixes the theorem as an append-only meta-fact
consistency boundary — seals the system at its unprovable consistency limit
